Definition: from G1211 and G4225; a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless:--verily.
BiblicalUsage: This is a small word of emphasis, the verily that makes a sentence land harder. It stands only once, in Hebrews, where the writer insists that Christ did not take on the nature of angels but the seed of Abraham.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that one small word can carry the whole gospel: Christ did not come as an angel looking on from above, but as a man, Abraham's seed, to take hold of us where we are.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
